memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They served him by himself, the brothers by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because Egyptians could not eat with Hebrews, for that is detestable to Egyptians." - Gen 43:32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At the meal, the seating reveals the divisions of that world. Joseph eats by himself, his brothers at a separate table, and the Egyptians at yet another — "because Egyptians could not eat with Hebrews." Cultural and ethnic barriers ran so deep that sharing a table across these lines was considered unthinkable, even "detestable." Even at a moment of reunion, the walls of society stood firm.

This small detail reflects a sad reality that runs through human history: people build walls between one another. Divisions of race, nationality, class, and culture separate people, deciding who may sit with whom, who is "us" and who is "them." These barriers are ancient, and they persist in our world still.

But the gospel brings a different vision. In Christ, the dividing walls come down. Jesus "himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility" (Eph 2:14). At the cross, God began forming a new people from every nation, who can sit together at one table as brothers and sisters. What Egyptian custom forbade, the grace of Christ makes possible.

This calls us to examine our own hearts. Are there "tables" we keep separate — people we quietly consider "not our kind"? God's heart is for reconciliation across every human divide. As people shaped by the gospel, may we work to tear down walls rather than build them, welcoming to our table those the world would keep apart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there people I quietly consider "not my kind"?
2. How does the gospel challenge the walls I might keep between people?
3. Where can I help tear down a dividing wall rather than reinforce it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You break down the walls that divide people. Examine my heart for any barriers I keep, and make me a person of reconciliation who welcomes to my table those the world would keep apart. Amen.
